newsitem.title: USA: Appliance Recycling may post near-breakeven Q1.
newsitem.headline: Appliance Recycling may post near-breakeven Q1.

text.p: Appliance Recycling Centers of America Inc said Thursday it may report first-quarter results ranging from near-breakeven to a small profit compared with a net loss of $1.9 million or $1.75 per share a year ago.

President Edward Cameron said the improvement is being driven by the impact of the company's reduced cost structure following consolidation of its Encore reconditioned appliance stores and above-plan sales of reconditioned appliances. He also cited expanded recycling volumes from Southern California Edison Co's demand-side energy conservation program.

Appliance Recycling reported a fourth-quarter loss of $3.0 million or $2.66 per share, which reflected one-time writeoffs and significant expenses related to consolidating its network of Encore reconditioned appliance stores and centers. This compared to a loss of $1 million or $0.99 per share a year ago.

The company's operating results for the fourth quarter were restated to reflect the impact of a one-for-four reverse stock split that became effective February 21, 1997. That action was taken to help keep the company in compliance with minimum stock price requirements of the Nasdaq Stock Market.
Cameron said the poor performance was due to difficulties related to repositioning the company in the appliance reuse market.

During the fourth quarter, the company withdrew from three underperforming markets by closing 12 retail stores and three recycling centers. It said significant expenses related to the consolidation caused it to post a substantially larger than planned net loss in the period.
